name: RELA fusion-positive ependymoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Histological features consistent with ependymoma including perivascular pseudorosettes
Detection of RELA fusion gene by molecular genetic testing (e.g., FISH, RT-PCR, or sequencing)
Tumor located in the supratentorial region of the brain on MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of ependymoma plus molecular confirmation of RELA fusion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing is essential to distinguish RELA fusion-positive ependymoma from other ependymoma subtypes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits related to supratentorial tumor location

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting associated with intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: feeling sick due to brain swelling

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances from increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vision problems with high brain pressure
weakness on one side of body
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

laboratory: CSF cytology typically negative for malignant cells
imaging: MRI showing supratentorial mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Possible cystic components and calcifications on imaging
other: Histopathology showing perivascular pseudorosettes and ependymal differentiation
Immunohistochemistry positive for L1CAM and nuclear p65/RELA expression

distinguishingFeatures: Tumor located in posterior fossa rather than supratentorial region
Histopathology showing astrocytic rather than ependymal differentiation

redFlags: New onset seizures in a child or young adult
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as persistent vomiting and papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Pajtler KW, et al. Molecular Classification of Ependymal Tumors across All CNS Compartments, Cancer Cell, 2015.
Witt H, et al. Delineation of Two Clinically and Molecularly Distinct Subgroups of Posterior Fossa Ependymoma, Cancer Cell, 2011.
